BlueprintResponse.description: A blueprint, with its own limits attached rather than implied.
BlueprintResponse.title: BlueprintResponse

EnqueueRunRequest.description:
``idempotency_key`` is required, not optional.

``MemoryService`` deduplicates on it, so a client that retries a request it
never saw the answer to converges on one run instead of two. Making it
optional would leave the one durable replay protection this API has to a
caller's discretion.
EnqueueRunRequest.title: EnqueueRunRequest

FindingResponse.description:
One quality finding.

No identifier, deliberately: findings are derived from state, not stored, so
there is nothing stable to address. A finding disappears when the condition
that produced it does (ADR-0015).
FindingResponse.title: FindingResponse

HealthResponse.description: FR-017. Reports without authentication and without leaking credentials.
HealthResponse.title: HealthResponse

KnowledgeResponse.description:
Carries every version, because history is the product.

A knowledge item that only exposes its current text would make the audit
trail invisible to the interface that exists to show it.
KnowledgeResponse.title: KnowledgeResponse

ReadinessResponse.description:
Everything needed to interrogate the number, never the number alone.

``is_stale`` is computed against the project's current revision at read time,
which is why it is not a stored status.
ReadinessResponse.title: ReadinessResponse

ResolvedResponse.description:
Whether the call changed anything.

``False`` means it was already resolved, which is not an error — a retried
resolution should be safe.
ResolvedResponse.title: ResolvedResponse

ReviewResponse.description: What a reviewer needs without inspecting the database (FR-015).
ReviewResponse.title: ReviewResponse

StatementResponse.description:
One blueprint statement.

Carries its knowledge item, so tracing it is one hop rather than a parallel
trace API over derived identifiers (ADR-0016). No statement lacks a label or
a trace target — FR-008's acceptance condition, and it holds structurally.
StatementResponse.title: StatementResponse

TraceResponse.description: A knowledge item's chain of custody: project, session, message, run, versions.
TraceResponse.title: TraceResponse

info.description:
Engineering memory for AI product discovery.

**This API has no authentication.** The MVP defers authentication, teams, and
roles, so it is safe only behind a network boundary (ADR-0014).

Long operations never hold a request open: enqueueing agent work returns `202`
with a durable run identifier, and the client polls the run.
info.title: KAE-Memory

get.description:
FR-017. Unversioned on purpose: an operational probe should not move
when the business contract does.

Reports ``degraded`` rather than ``ok`` when the database is unreachable,
and never returns a connection string — the URL contains the password.

post.description:
Confirm a candidate.

Confirmation is a human act. No agent performs it, which is why this is an
endpoint and not a step inside a run.

get.description:
Return a knowledge item's chain of custody.

Project, the sessions and messages it came from, the run that produced it,
the runs that consumed it, and every version with its provenance — the answer
to "why does the blueprint say this?"

schema.title: Response List Projects V1 Projects Get
Response List Blockers V1 Projects  Project Id  Blockers Get

post.description: Record something that must be closed before a blueprint is credible.

get.description:
Render confirmed knowledge as a blueprint.

Returned even below the draft threshold, marked incomplete. Refusing would
tell a user nothing about *what is missing*, and for an early project the
missing-area list is the most useful thing the blueprint can say.

Every statement is a confirmed knowledge item's own text. No model writes
blueprint prose (ADR-0016), because generated connective text would be
unattributable — the failure FR-008's labelling exists to prevent.

Export the same blueprint as Markdown (FR-008).

A rendering of the same structure the JSON exposes, so the two cannot
disagree. Every statement keeps its label and knowledge identifier, so an
exported document is as traceable as the API response.

post.description:
Record that two knowledge items contradict each other.

An unresolved contradiction touching a mandatory area blocks readiness, which
is what makes this more than an annotation.

Resolve a contradiction.

``resolved: false`` means it was already settled. That is not an error — a
retried resolution has to be safe — and the edge is never deleted, because a
contradiction that was raised and closed is part of the audit trail.

get.description:
List a project's knowledge.

Unfiltered by default. The workspace needs to show proposed candidates beside
confirmed knowledge, because the difference between them is the thing a user
acts on.

schema.title: Response List Knowledge V1 Projects  Project Id  Knowledge Get

get.description:
Return the latest snapshot, calculating one if none exists.

Calculating on first read rather than returning 404 means the workspace shows
a real zero for an untouched project instead of an error it would have to
explain.

post.description:
Link a knowledge item to a discovery area.

An authoritative change: it alters which areas an item can cover, so the
project's knowledge revision advances and earlier snapshots go stale.

Recalculate and append a snapshot.

Appends rather than replaces. Readiness history is how the product shows
readiness *moving* as knowledge is confirmed.

schema.title: Response Readiness History V1 Projects  Project Id  Readiness History Get

get.description:
Return quality findings, most severe first (FR-015).

Derived from operational data on every request rather than stored, so the
findings can never disagree with the state they describe. Acting on one means
changing that state — confirm the knowledge, assign the area, resolve the
contradiction — and the finding disappears.
List a project's execution history, most recent first.

schema.title: Response List Runs V1 Projects  Project Id  Runs Get

post.description:
Enqueue agent work and return immediately.

**202, never 200.** The run is durable when this returns, but it has not
started: a worker claims it. The browser does not own the run (ADR-0009), so
closing the tab cannot lose it.

Idempotent on ``idempotency_key`` — a retried request converges on the
original run rather than creating a second.

schema.title: Response List Sessions V1 Projects  Project Id  Sessions Get

get.description: Return one run. This is what a client polls while work proceeds.

Stream run progress as Server-Sent Events.

A convenience over ``GET /v1/runs/{id}``, never a replacement for it.
Correctness must not depend on an uninterrupted browser connection
(ADR-0009), so a client that misses the stream entirely can still read the
same state with an ordinary request.

Emits the current state immediately, then on every change to status,
attempt, checkpoint, or error. Closes when the run reaches a terminal
status.

Return the knowledge a run produced.

One run, one result: replaying a completed run returns its original output
rather than producing a second set.

schema.title: Response Knowledge Produced By V1 Runs  Run Id  Knowledge Get

get.description: List a session's messages in submission order.

schema.title: Response List Messages V1 Sessions  Session Id  Messages Get

post.description:
Record a message verbatim as source evidence.

The stored text is never rewritten by extraction, so the original wording
stays available as the source of anything derived from it.
